newsitem.title: Moldova: Moldova and Ukraine agree to form customs union.
newsitem.headline: Moldova and Ukraine agree to form customs union.

text.p: Presidents Leonid Kuchma of Ukraine and Petru Lucinschi of Moldova pledged on Tuesday to form an "equal" customs union removing many barriers between their countries.
The move is likely to be seen as rivalling Russian-led pacts with other former Soviet republics which Moldova and Ukraine have kept out of.
"We are taking a step towards a higher level of relations. Many barriers are being removed," Kuchma said after signing a signed a customs union declaration in the Moldovan capital.
Neither president referred specifically to customs deals between Russia and other former Soviet republics, but the agreement underlined their sensitivities over ties with Moscow.

"There is one thing that is different about our union -- it is a union of equal states, equal sides. This is its essence," Kuchma said of the union, under which transit fees and duties are to be lifted between the neighbouring countries.

Lucinschi, elected three months ago in the country of 4.3 million people on promises of better ties with Russia, said the union -- due to come into force by the end of this year -- was not aimed against anyone.
"Our will to form a customs union doesn't damage any third country. It will only help to develop ties, for instance, with Russia or Belarus," he said.

Ukraine and Moldova have been sceptical about fast and deep integration in the 12-member Commonwealth of Independent States, formed on the ashes of the Soviet Union, and have not joined a customs union of Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan.
Ukraine, which has a population of more than 50 million, has also criticised a "community" planned by Russia and Belarus in their drive for closer integration.

Ukraine's top security official said in Chisinau that Moldova and separatists in rebel Dnestr had asked Ukraine to send peacekeepers to the breakaway region to reinforce Russian forces deployed there.
Volodymyr Horbulin said Dnestr separatist leader Igor Smirnov had made the request and also asked Kiev to send military observers.
"Igor Smirnov has proposed that Ukrainian peacekeeping troops are sent to the Dnestr region," Horbulin, head of Ukraine's Security and Defence Council, told reporters.
"Moldova also backs this idea," he said.
Moldovan and Dnestr officials were not immediately available to comment.
Slav separatist leaders declared Dnestr independent in 1990, but no other country has recognised the sliver of industrial land in eastern Moldova as an independent state.
Fighting erupted between Moldovan forces and the Dnestr separatists in 1992, killing hundreds of people before Russian troops intervened to halt the conflict.
The political conflict remains unresolved. Moldova says it is ready to grant broad autonomy to Dnestr, but the separatist leaders still want full independence.

About 6,000 Russian troops are still deployed in Dnestr, in eastern Moldova bordering Ukraine. Russia agreed to pull its troops out under a deal signed in 1994, but says it will withdraw them only when the political conflict is resolved.
Up to 200,000 ethnic Ukrainians live in Dnestr and Ukraine has strong economic links with the region.
